review.source: Actual written N1904 and the publisher rows, reviewed against the displayed BSB by Claude (Anthropic); independent peer review recorded in the registry.

15:1.sourceText: Καὶ εὐθὺς πρωῒ συμβούλιον ἑτοιμάσαντες οἱ ἀρχιερεῖς μετὰ τῶν πρεσβυτέρων καὶ γραμματέων καὶ ὅλον τὸ συνέδριον, δήσαντες τὸν Ἰησοῦν ἀπήνεγκαν καὶ παρέδωκαν Πειλάτῳ.
15:1.targetText: Early in the morning, the chief priests, elders, scribes, and the whole Sanhedrin devised a plan. They bound Jesus, led Him away, and handed Him over to Pilate.

groups.note: πρωΐ itself means early in the morning, as in Mark 1:35.
The participle ἑτοιμάσαντες "having prepared" is rendered devised; the publisher's Greek reads ποιήσαντες (having made), with the same sense here.
The one object τὸν Ἰησοῦν serves all three verbs; BSB repeats it as Him.
The dative Πειλάτῳ is rendered to Pilate.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the opening connective καί untranslated.
BSB leaves εὐθύς (immediately) untranslated.
BSB turns "with the elders" into a list; μετά and its article have no separate English word.
The καί joining elders and scribes is represented by a comma in BSB's list.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

15:2.sourceText: καὶ ἐπηρώτησεν αὐτὸν ὁ Πειλᾶτος Σὺ εἶ ὁ Βασιλεὺς τῶν Ἰουδαίων; ὁ δὲ ἀποκριθεὶς αὐτῷ λέγει Σὺ λέγεις.
15:2.targetText: So Pilate questioned Him, “Are You the King of the Jews?”  “You have said so,” Jesus replied.

groups.note: The article ὁ used as a pronoun, "he", is rendered by the name Jesus.
ἀποκριθεὶς … λέγει "answering says" is rendered replied.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB leaves the connective δέ untranslated.
BSB does not render αὐτῷ (to him) after replied.

15:3.sourceText: καὶ κατηγόρουν αὐτοῦ οἱ ἀρχιερεῖς πολλά.
15:3.targetText: And the chief priests began to accuse Him of many things.

groups.note: The imperfect κατηγόρουν is rendered began to accuse.

15:4.sourceText: ὁ δὲ Πειλᾶτος πάλιν ἐπηρώτα αὐτὸν λέγων Οὐκ ἀποκρίνῃ οὐδέν; ἴδε πόσα σου κατηγοροῦσιν.
15:4.targetText: Then Pilate questioned Him again, “Have You no answer? Look how many charges they are bringing against You!”

groups.note: The double negative Οὐκ … οὐδέν "not … anything" is rendered no.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
The participle λέγων (saying) is represented only by the comma before the quotation.

15:5.sourceText: ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς οὐκέτι οὐδὲν ἀπεκρίθη, ὥστε θαυμάζειν τὸν Πειλᾶτον.
15:5.targetText: But to Pilate’s amazement, Jesus made no further reply.

groups.note: οὐκέτι οὐδέν "no longer anything" is rendered no further.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

15:6.sourceText: Κατὰ δὲ ἑορτὴν ἀπέλυεν αὐτοῖς ἕνα δέσμιον ὃν παρῃτοῦντο.
15:6.targetText: Now it was Pilate’s custom at the feast to release to the people a prisoner of their choosing.

groups.note: The customary imperfect ἀπέλυεν "he used to release" is rendered it was … custom … to release.
The pronoun αὐτοῖς (to them) is rendered to the people.
ὃν παρῃτοῦντο "whom they requested" is rendered of their choosing.

unmappedTarget.reason: English names Pilate; the Greek gives him only in the verb ending of ἀπέλυεν.

15:7.sourceText: ἦν δὲ ὁ λεγόμενος Βαραββᾶς μετὰ τῶν στασιαστῶν δεδεμένος, οἵτινες ἐν τῇ στάσει φόνον πεποιήκεισαν.
15:7.targetText: And a man named Barabbas was imprisoned with the rebels who had committed murder during the insurrection.

groups.note: The article with the participle, "the one called", is rendered a man named.

15:8.sourceText: καὶ ἀναβὰς ὁ ὄχλος ἤρξατο αἰτεῖσθαι καθὼς ἐποίει αὐτοῖς.
15:8.targetText: So the crowd went up and began asking Pilate to keep his custom.

groups.note: καθὼς ἐποίει "as he used to do" is rendered to keep his custom.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB does not render αὐτοῖς (for them) after his custom.

unmappedTarget.reason: English coordinator; the participle ἀναβάς is rendered as a finite verb, went up.
English supplies the one asked; αἰτεῖσθαι has no object in Greek.

15:9.sourceText: ὁ δὲ Πειλᾶτος ἀπεκρίθη αὐτοῖς λέγων Θέλετε ἀπολύσω ὑμῖν τὸν Βασιλέα τῶν Ἰουδαίων;
15:9.targetText: “Do you want me to release to you the King of the Jews?” Pilate asked.

groups.note: ἀπεκρίθη … λέγων "answered … saying" is rendered asked.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB leaves the connective δέ untranslated.
BSB does not render αὐτοῖς (to them) after asked.

15:10.sourceText: ἐγίνωσκεν γὰρ ὅτι διὰ φθόνον παραδεδώκεισαν αὐτὸν οἱ ἀρχιερεῖς.
15:10.targetText: For he knew it was out of envy that the chief priests had handed Jesus over.

groups.note: The pronoun αὐτόν (him) is rendered by the name Jesus.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies a cleft frame to focus out of envy; the Greek has none.

15:11.sourceText: οἱ δὲ ἀρχιερεῖς ἀνέσεισαν τὸν ὄχλον ἵνα μᾶλλον τὸν Βαραββᾶν ἀπολύσῃ αὐτοῖς.
15:11.targetText: But the chief priests stirred up the crowd to have him release Barabbas to them instead.

groups.note: The subjunctive ἀπολύσῃ "that he should release" is rendered have him release.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

15:12.sourceText: ὁ δὲ Πειλᾶτος πάλιν ἀποκριθεὶς ἔλεγεν αὐτοῖς Τί οὖν ποιήσω ὃν λέγετε τὸν Βασιλέα τῶν Ἰουδαίων;
15:12.targetText: So Pilate asked them again, “What then do you want me to do with the One you call the King of the Jews?”

groups.note: ἀποκριθεὶς … ἔλεγεν "answering said" is rendered asked.
The relative ὅν (whom) is rendered with the One.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: The publisher's Greek has θέλετε (do you want) here; N1904 lacks it.

15:13.sourceText: οἱ δὲ πάλιν ἔκραξαν Σταύρωσον αὐτόν.

groups.note: The article οἱ used as a pronoun is rendered they.
πάλιν "again" is rendered back, of a shouted reply.

15:14.sourceText: ὁ δὲ Πειλᾶτος ἔλεγεν αὐτοῖς Τί γὰρ ἐποίησεν κακόν; οἱ δὲ περισσῶς ἔκραξαν Σταύρωσον αὐτόν.
15:14.targetText: “Why?” asked Pilate. “What evil has He done?”  But they shouted all the louder, “Crucify Him!”

groups.note: γάρ in a retort ("Why, what evil …?") is rendered as the separate question Why.
The article οἱ used as a pronoun is rendered they.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB leaves the connective δέ untranslated.
BSB does not render αὐτοῖς (to them) after asked.

15:15.sourceText: ὁ δὲ Πειλᾶτος βουλόμενος τῷ ὄχλῳ τὸ ἱκανὸν ποιῆσαι ἀπέλυσεν αὐτοῖς τὸν Βαραββᾶν, καὶ παρέδωκεν τὸν Ἰησοῦν φραγελλώσας ἵνα σταυρωθῇ.
15:15.targetText: And wishing to satisfy the crowd, Pilate released Barabbas to them. But he had Jesus flogged, and handed Him over to be crucified.

groups.note: τὸ ἱκανὸν ποιῆσαι "to do what is enough" is an idiom for to satisfy.
The καί here introduces a contrasting action and is rendered But.
The one object τὸν Ἰησοῦν serves both verbs; BSB repeats it as Him.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English coordinator; the participle φραγελλώσας is rendered as had … flogged.

15:16.sourceText: Οἱ δὲ στρατιῶται ἀπήγαγον αὐτὸν ἔσω τῆς αὐλῆς, ὅ ἐστιν Πραιτώριον, καὶ συνκαλοῦσιν ὅλην τὴν σπεῖραν.
15:16.targetText: Then the soldiers led Jesus away into the palace (that is, the Praetorium) and called the whole company together.

groups.note: The pronoun αὐτόν (him) is rendered by the name Jesus.
συνκαλοῦσιν "they call together" is rendered called … together.

15:17.sourceText: καὶ ἐνδιδύσκουσιν αὐτὸν πορφύραν καὶ περιτιθέασιν αὐτῷ πλέξαντες ἀκάνθινον στέφανον·
15:17.targetText: They dressed Him in a purple robe, twisted together a crown of thorns, and set it on His head.

groups.note: The dative αὐτῷ "(around) Him" is rendered His, with head supplied.
The one object στέφανον serves both πλέξαντες and περιτιθέασιν; BSB resumes it as it.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the opening connective καί untranslated.

unmappedTarget.reason: English names where the crown was set; the Greek says only "around Him".

15:18.sourceText: καὶ ἤρξαντο ἀσπάζεσθαι αὐτόν Χαῖρε, Βασιλεῦ τῶν Ἰουδαίων·
15:18.targetText: And they began to salute Him: “Hail, King of the Jews!”

15:19.sourceText: καὶ ἔτυπτον αὐτοῦ τὴν κεφαλὴν καλάμῳ καὶ ἐνέπτυον αὐτῷ, καὶ τιθέντες τὰ γόνατα προσεκύνουν αὐτῷ.
15:19.targetText: They kept striking His head with a staff and spitting on Him. And they knelt down and bowed before Him.

groups.note: The imperfect ἔτυπτον is rendered kept striking.
τιθέντες τὰ γόνατα "placing the knees" is rendered knelt down.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the opening connective καί untranslated.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English coordinator; the participle τιθέντες is rendered as a finite verb, knelt down.

15:20.sourceText: καὶ ὅτε ἐνέπαιξαν αὐτῷ, ἐξέδυσαν αὐτὸν τὴν πορφύραν καὶ ἐνέδυσαν αὐτὸν τὰ ἱμάτια αὐτοῦ. Καὶ ἐξάγουσιν αὐτὸν ἵνα σταυρώσωσιν αὐτόν.
15:20.targetText: After they had mocked Him, they removed the purple robe and put His own clothes back on Him. Then they led Him out to crucify Him.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the opening connective καί untranslated.
BSB does not render αὐτόν, the person stripped of the robe.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: The publisher's Greek has one word here that N1904 lacks, which BSB renders own.
English adds back; the Greek says only that they clothed Him in His garments.

15:21.sourceText: καὶ ἀγγαρεύουσιν παράγοντά τινα Σίμωνα Κυρηναῖον ἐρχόμενον ἀπ’ ἀγροῦ, τὸν πατέρα Ἀλεξάνδρου καὶ Ῥούφου, ἵνα ἄρῃ τὸν σταυρὸν αὐτοῦ.
15:21.targetText: Now Simon of Cyrene, the father of Alexander and Rufus, was passing by on his way in from the country, and the soldiers forced him to carry the cross of Jesus.

groups.note: The verse-opening καί is rendered Now.
The participle παράγοντα is rendered as a finite verb, was passing by.
Σίμωνα is the object of ἀγγαρεύουσιν; BSB makes Simon the subject of its own clause and resumes him as the object.
The pronoun αὐτοῦ (his) is rendered of Jesus.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves τινα (a certain man) untranslated; the name Simon identifies him.

unmappedTarget.reason: English coordinator joining BSB's two clauses; the Greek has a participle, not a conjunction.
English names the subject; the Greek gives it only in the verb ending of ἀγγαρεύουσιν.

15:22.sourceText: καὶ φέρουσιν αὐτὸν ἐπὶ τὸν Γολγοθᾶν τόπον, ὅ ἐστιν μεθερμηνευόμενος Κρανίου τόπος.
15:22.targetText: They brought Jesus to a place called Golgotha, which means The Place of the Skull.

groups.note: The pronoun αὐτόν (him) is rendered by the name Jesus.
ἐστιν μεθερμηνευόμενος "is, translated" is rendered means; the publisher's Greek has the neuter μεθερμηνευόμενον, same sense.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the opening connective καί untranslated.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies called; the Greek puts the name Golgotha before τόπον without a verb.

15:23.sourceText: καὶ ἐδίδουν αὐτῷ ἐσμυρνισμένον οἶνον· ὃς δὲ οὐκ ἔλαβεν.
15:23.targetText: There they offered Him wine mixed with myrrh, but He did not take it.

groups.note: The imperfect ἐδίδουν is rendered offered.
The relative ὅς with δέ, "but he", is rendered He.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the opening connective καί untranslated.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the place word (Golgotha); the Greek has no locative adverb.
English supplies an object; ἔλαβεν has none in Greek.

15:24.sourceText: καὶ σταυροῦσιν αὐτὸν, καὶ διαμερίζονται τὰ ἱμάτια αὐτοῦ, βάλλοντες κλῆρον ἐπ’ αὐτὰ τίς τί ἄρῃ.
15:24.targetText: And they crucified Him.  They also divided His garments by casting lots to decide what each of them would take.

groups.note: The καί joining the clauses is rendered also.
The interrogative τίς "who" is rendered each of them.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB does not render ἐπ’ αὐτά (over them, the garments).

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies a frame for the indirect question τίς τί ἄρῃ.

15:25.sourceText: ἦν δὲ ὥρα τρίτη καὶ ἐσταύρωσαν αὐτόν.
15:25.targetText: It was the third hour when they crucified Him.

groups.note: BSB joins the two clauses with when, rendering καί.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the connective δέ untranslated.

15:26.sourceText: καὶ ἦν ἡ ἐπιγραφὴ τῆς αἰτίας αὐτοῦ ἐπιγεγραμμένη Ο ΒΑΣΙΛΕΥΣ ΤΩΝ ΙΟΥΔΑΙΩΝ.
15:26.targetText: And the charge inscribed against Him read:  THE KING OF THE JEWS.

groups.note: The periphrastic ἦν … ἐπιγεγραμμένη "was inscribed" is rendered read.
The noun ἐπιγραφή "inscription" is rendered by the participle inscribed.
αὐτοῦ "his" (the charge against him) is rendered against Him.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

15:27.sourceText: Καὶ σὺν αὐτῷ σταυροῦσιν δύο λῃστάς, ἕνα ἐκ δεξιῶν καὶ ἕνα ἐξ εὐωνύμων αὐτοῦ.
15:27.targetText: Along with Jesus, they crucified two robbers, one on His right and one on His left.

groups.note: The pronoun αὐτῷ (him) is rendered by the name Jesus.
The one αὐτοῦ (his) applies to both sides; BSB repeats His.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the opening connective καί untranslated.

15:29.sourceText: Καὶ οἱ παραπορευόμενοι ἐβλασφήμουν αὐτὸν κινοῦντες τὰς κεφαλὰς αὐτῶν καὶ λέγοντες Οὐὰ ὁ καταλύων τὸν ναὸν καὶ οἰκοδομῶν ἐν τρισὶν ἡμέραις,
15:29.targetText: And those who passed by heaped abuse on Him, shaking their heads and saying, “Aha! You who are going to destroy the temple and rebuild it in three days,

groups.note: The article with the participle, "the ones passing by", is rendered those who passed by.

targetPhrases.text: You who are going to destroy

groups.note: The articular participle ὁ καταλύων is a form of address, "you who destroy".

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies an object; οἰκοδομῶν has none in Greek.

15:30.sourceText: σῶσον σεαυτὸν καταβὰς ἀπὸ τοῦ σταυροῦ.
15:30.targetText: come down from the cross and save Yourself!”

groups.note: The participle καταβάς is rendered as a command, come down.

unmappedTarget.reason: English coordinator; the participle καταβάς is rendered as a command joined to save.

15:31.sourceText: ὁμοίως καὶ οἱ ἀρχιερεῖς ἐμπαίζοντες πρὸς ἀλλήλους μετὰ τῶν γραμματέων ἔλεγον Ἄλλους ἔσωσεν, ἑαυτὸν οὐ δύναται σῶσαι·
15:31.targetText: In the same way, the chief priests and scribes mocked Him among themselves, saying, “He saved others, but He cannot save Himself!

groups.note: μετά "with" (the scribes) is rendered and, making the scribes a second subject.
The imperfect ἔλεγον "were saying" is rendered by the participle saying.
οὐ δύναται "is not able" is rendered by the single English word cannot.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves καί (also) untranslated after In the same way.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies an object; ἐμπαίζοντες has none in Greek.
English coordinator; the Greek clauses are joined without a conjunction.

15:32.sourceText: ὁ Χριστὸς ὁ Βασιλεὺς Ἰσραὴλ καταβάτω νῦν ἀπὸ τοῦ σταυροῦ, ἵνα ἴδωμεν καὶ πιστεύσωμεν. καὶ οἱ συνεσταυρωμένοι σὺν αὐτῷ ὠνείδιζον αὐτόν.
15:32.targetText: Let the Christ, the King of Israel, come down now from the cross, so that we may see and believe!” And even those who were crucified with Him berated Him.

groups.note: The third-person imperative καταβάτω is rendered Let … come down.
The one καί serves both as the connective and as even.
The article with the participle, "the ones crucified with", is rendered those who were crucified.

15:33.sourceText: Καὶ γενομένης ὥρας ἕκτης σκότος ἐγένετο ἐφ’ ὅλην τὴν γῆν ἕως ὥρας ἐνάτης.
15:33.targetText: From the sixth hour until the ninth hour darkness came over all the land.

groups.note: The genitive absolute γενομένης ὥρας ἕκτης "when the sixth hour came" is rendered From the sixth hour.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the opening connective καί untranslated.

15:34.sourceText: καὶ τῇ ἐνάτῃ ὥρᾳ ἐβόησεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς φωνῇ μεγάλῃ Ἐλωῒ Ἐλωῒ λαμὰ σαβαχθανεί; ὅ ἐστιν μεθερμηνευόμενον Ὁ Θεός μου ὁ Θεός μου, εἰς τί ἐγκατέλιπές με;
15:34.targetText: At the ninth hour, Jesus cried out in a loud voice, “Eloi, Eloi, lema sabachthani?” which means, “My God, My God, why have You forsaken Me?”

groups.note: BSB transliterates the publisher's spelling λεμα; N1904 spells the same Aramaic word λαμά.
The publisher's Greek spells this σαβαχθανι; N1904 has σαβαχθανεί, the same word.
ἐστιν μεθερμηνευόμενον "is, translated" is rendered means.
εἰς τί "for what" is rendered why.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the opening connective καί untranslated.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

15:35.sourceText: καί τινες τῶν παρεστηκότων ἀκούσαντες ἔλεγον Ἴδε Ἡλείαν φωνεῖ.
15:35.targetText: When some of those standing nearby heard this, they said, “Behold, He is calling Elijah.”

groups.note: The article with the participle, "the ones standing by", is rendered those standing nearby.
The participle ἀκούσαντες is rendered as a When-clause.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the opening connective καί untranslated.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies an object for heard; the Greek has none.

15:36.sourceText: δραμὼν δέ τις καὶ γεμίσας σπόγγον ὄξους περιθεὶς καλάμῳ ἐπότιζεν αὐτόν, λέγων Ἄφετε ἴδωμεν εἰ ἔρχεται Ἡλείας καθελεῖν αὐτόν.
15:36.targetText: And someone ran and filled a sponge with sour wine. He put it on a reed and held it up for Jesus to drink, saying, “Leave Him alone. Let us see if Elijah comes to take Him down.”

groups.note: The imperfect ἐπότιζεν "gave him a drink" is rendered held … up for … to drink.
The pronoun αὐτόν (him) is rendered by the name Jesus.
Ἄφετε "let be" is rendered Leave … alone.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies an object pronoun for the sponge; περιθείς has none in Greek.
English coordinator; the participle περιθείς is rendered as a finite verb, put.
English supplies an object pronoun for the sponge; the Greek has none.
English supplies an object; Ἄφετε has none in Greek.

15:37.sourceText: ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς ἀφεὶς φωνὴν μεγάλην ἐξέπνευσεν.
15:37.targetText: But Jesus let out a loud cry and breathed His last.

groups.note: ἐξέπνευσεν "breathed out" is rendered breathed His last.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English coordinator; the participle ἀφείς is rendered as a finite verb, let out.

15:38.sourceText: Καὶ τὸ καταπέτασμα τοῦ ναοῦ ἐσχίσθη εἰς δύο ἀπ’ ἄνωθεν ἕως κάτω.
15:38.targetText: And the veil of the temple was torn in two from top to bottom.

15:39.sourceText: Ἰδὼν δὲ ὁ κεντυρίων ὁ παρεστηκὼς ἐξ ἐναντίας αὐτοῦ ὅτι οὕτως ἐξέπνευσεν, εἶπεν Ἀληθῶς οὗτος ὁ ἄνθρωπος Υἱὸς Θεοῦ ἦν.
15:39.targetText: When the centurion standing there in front of Jesus saw how He had breathed His last, he said, “Truly this man was the Son of God!”

groups.note: The participle Ἰδών is rendered as a When-clause.
The article with the participle, "the one standing by", is rendered standing there.
ἐξ ἐναντίας "from opposite" is rendered in front of.
The pronoun αὐτοῦ (him) is rendered by the name Jesus.
ὅτι οὕτως "that in this way" is rendered how.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the connective δέ untranslated.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

15:40.sourceText: Ἦσαν δὲ καὶ γυναῖκες ἀπὸ μακρόθεν θεωροῦσαι, ἐν αἷς καὶ Μαρία ἡ Μαγδαληνὴ καὶ Μαρία ἡ Ἰακώβου τοῦ μικροῦ καὶ Ἰωσῆτος μήτηρ καὶ Σαλώμη,
15:40.targetText: And there were also women watching from a distance. Among them were Mary Magdalene, Mary the mother of James the younger and of Joses, and Salome.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves καί (also) in "among whom also" untranslated.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
The καί joining the first two names is represented by a comma in BSB's list.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the verb; the Greek clause ἐν αἷς … is verbless.

15:41.sourceText: αἳ ὅτε ἦν ἐν τῇ Γαλιλαίᾳ ἠκολούθουν αὐτῷ καὶ διηκόνουν αὐτῷ, καὶ ἄλλαι πολλαὶ αἱ συναναβᾶσαι αὐτῷ εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα.
15:41.targetText: These women had followed Jesus and ministered to Him while He was in Galilee, and there were many other women who had come up to Jerusalem with Him.

groups.note: The relative αἵ (who) is rendered These women.
The pronoun αὐτῷ (him) is rendered by the name Jesus.
The article with the participle, "the women who came up with", is rendered women who had come up.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies a verb; the Greek phrase ἄλλαι πολλαί is verbless.

15:42.sourceText: Καὶ ἤδη ὀψίας γενομένης, ἐπεὶ ἦν Παρασκευή, ὅ ἐστιν προσάββατον,
15:42.targetText: Now it was already evening. Since it was Preparation Day (that is, the day before the Sabbath),

groups.note: The genitive absolute ὀψίας γενομένης "evening having come" is rendered it was … evening.

15:43.sourceText: ἐλθὼν Ἰωσὴφ ὁ ἀπὸ Ἀριμαθαίας, εὐσχήμων βουλευτής, ὃς καὶ αὐτὸς ἦν προσδεχόμενος τὴν βασιλείαν τοῦ Θεοῦ, τολμήσας εἰσῆλθεν πρὸς τὸν Πειλᾶτον καὶ ᾐτήσατο τὸ σῶμα τοῦ Ἰησοῦ.
15:43.targetText: Joseph of Arimathea, a prominent Council member who himself was waiting for the kingdom of God, boldly went to Pilate to ask for the body of Jesus.

groups.note: ἐλθών … εἰσῆλθεν "coming … went in" is rendered by the one verb went.
The participle τολμήσας "having dared" is rendered boldly.
The finite ᾐτήσατο "asked for" is rendered as the purpose phrase to ask for.

15:44.sourceText: ὁ δὲ Πειλᾶτος ἐθαύμασεν εἰ ἤδη τέθνηκεν, καὶ προσκαλεσάμενος τὸν κεντυρίωνα ἐπηρώτησεν αὐτὸν εἰ πάλαι ἀπέθανεν·
15:44.targetText: Pilate was surprised to hear that Jesus was already dead, so he summoned the centurion to ask if this was so.

groups.note: The perfect τέθνηκεν "has died" is rendered was dead.
The finite ἐπηρώτησεν "asked" is rendered as the purpose phrase to ask.

πάλαι ἀπέθανεν ("he had died some time ago"): BSB does not render the repeated content and asks with the pro-form "if this was so" instead.

15:45.sourceText: καὶ γνοὺς ἀπὸ τοῦ κεντυρίωνος ἐδωρήσατο τὸ πτῶμα τῷ Ἰωσήφ.
15:45.targetText: When Pilate had confirmed it with the centurion, he granted the body to Joseph.

groups.note: The participle γνούς "having learned" is rendered as a When-clause.
The dative τῷ Ἰωσήφ is rendered to Joseph.

15:46.sourceText: καὶ ἀγοράσας σινδόνα καθελὼν αὐτὸν ἐνείλησεν τῇ σινδόνι καὶ κατέθηκεν αὐτὸν ἐν μνήματι ὃ ἦν λελατομημένον ἐκ πέτρας, καὶ προσεκύλισεν λίθον ἐπὶ τὴν θύραν τοῦ μνημείου.
15:46.targetText: So Joseph bought a linen cloth, took down the body of Jesus, wrapped it in the cloth, and placed it in a tomb that had been cut out of the rock. Then he rolled a stone against the entrance to the tomb.

groups.note: The pronoun αὐτόν (him) is rendered the body of Jesus, and BSB repeats it as it with wrapped.
κατέθηκεν "laid down" is rendered placed; the publisher's Greek reads ἔθηκεν (laid), same sense.
N1904 μνήματι and the publisher's μνημείῳ are synonyms, both meaning tomb.

15:47.sourceText: ἡ δὲ Μαρία ἡ Μαγδαληνὴ καὶ Μαρία ἡ Ἰωσῆτος ἐθεώρουν ποῦ τέθειται.
15:47.targetText: Mary Magdalene and Mary the mother of Joseph saw where His body was placed.

groups.note: The article ἡ with the genitive Ἰωσῆτος, "the (mother) of Joses", stands for mother; 15:40 writes μήτηρ.
Ἰωσῆτος is the genitive of Ἰωσῆς (Joses, as in 15:40), a form of the name Joseph.
